findings.claim: S2 md:71 'It also closed back at its level on the S&P 500's high day, after its lowest point in the episode, sooner in each: 55 trading days against 126, 505 against 513, and 51 against 89.'
findings.evidence: Figures are right under the computed rule: my scratch checks.py (imports build_analysis readers, episode_table) gives counts from the S&P 500 high of 126/55, 513/505, 89/51, equal to results.json episodes[*].*.regain_days, and the closing-back dates are earlier for Bitcoin in each (2020-05-07 vs 2020-08-18, 2024-01-08 vs 2024-01-19, 2025-05-02 vs 2025-06-27), so 'sooner' holds by date. But the sentence never says where the count starts. Round 2's insertion 'after its lowest point in the episode' now sits right before 'sooner ... 55 trading days', making the asset's low the nearest anchor. Counting from each asset's own low (same script): Bitcoin 39, 325, 17 trading days; S&P 500 103, 318, 55. Only the sh-3 footnote (make_charts.py:195-196, 'counts S&P 500 trading days from the high') states the anchor; the prose does not. Pronoun 'its' (both uses) resolves to Bitcoin; for the S&P 500 both readings of 'its lowest point' coincide with the trough. See finding R3-B1.
